stimuli.title: Three symbol codes for relations
stimuli.solution: Decode pair by pair from the left; the parents of a child are a married couple.

stimuli.title: A family described in three codes
stimuli.content:
In a certain code, 'A ⊕ B' means 'A is a parent of B', 'A ⊗ B' means 'A is married to B' and 'A ⊖ B' means 'A and B are siblings'. Kartik, Mehul, Pranav and Qasim are male; Leela, Naina, Ojasvi and Riya are female. The following are true:

- Kartik ⊗ Leela
- Leela ⊕ Mehul
- Mehul ⊖ Naina
- Ojasvi ⊗ Mehul
- Ojasvi ⊕ Pranav
- Qasim ⊗ Naina
- Qasim ⊕ Riya
stimuli.solution:
Leela, Kartik's wife, is a parent of Mehul, and Naina is Mehul's sibling, so both are children of Kartik and Leela. Ojasvi is Mehul's wife and Pranav's mother; Qasim is Naina's husband and Riya's parent.
Tree: Kartik + Leela → Mehul (+ Ojasvi) → Pranav; Naina (+ Qasim) → Riya.

stimuli.title: A taxi's route with five stops
stimuli.content: A taxi leaves its depot D and drives in straight lines: 6 km east to stop A, then 8 km north to stop B, then 12 km west to stop C, then 5 km south to stop E, and finally 10 km east to stop F, where it ends its trip.
stimuli.solution: With D at (0, 0), east and north positive: A (6, 0), B (6, 8), C (−6, 8), E (−6, 3), F (4, 3).

stimuli.title: Six points with a midpoint
stimuli.content:
Six points J, K, L, M, N and O lie on flat ground.

- J is 10 m east of K.
- L is 10 m north of J.
- M is the midpoint of the straight line joining K and L.
- N is 5 m south of M.
- O is 7 m west of M.

stimuli.title: A three-part code that depends on word length
stimuli.content:
In a certain code, a word is written as: its last letter, then the number of letters in the word, then the letter that comes two places after its first letter in the English alphabet. If the word has an even number of letters, the whole code is then written in reverse order.
For example, TRAIN is written as N5V and HOME is written as J4E.
stimuli.solution: Odd length: last letter + length + (first letter + 2). Even length: the same three parts, reversed.

stimuli.title: Arrangement of 17 elements beginning with W

W 3 % H 8 A @ 5 K £ 1 F 7 I # 2 Y
stimuli.solution: Number the elements 1 to 17 from the left; the k-th from the right is the (18 − k)-th from the left.

stimuli.title: Arrangement of 24 elements beginning with M
stimuli.content:
Study the following arrangement of letters, numbers and symbols and answer the question.

M 4 & D U 7 © S 2 E # K 9 V £ 3 A Z 6 % H O 8 $
stimuli.solution: Number the elements 1 to 24 from the left (k-th from the right = (25 − k)-th from the left). Vowels: U, E, A, O.

stimuli.title: Arrangement of 30 elements beginning with 5
stimuli.content:
Study the following arrangement of letters, numbers and symbols and answer the question.

5 Q @ E 8 J % 2 I N 7 # T 4 & O P 3 £ G A 9 ¥ L 6 K * U 1 R
stimuli.solution: Number the elements 1 to 30 from the left (k-th from the right = (31 − k)-th from the left). Vowels: E, I, O, A, U. When elements are removed or regrouped, write out the new arrangement before counting.

stimuli.title: Questions on the word REPUBLICANS
stimuli.content:
Answer the questions on the basis of the word given below.

R E P U B L I C A N S
stimuli.solution: Alphabetical positions: R 18, E 5, P 16, U 21, B 2, L 12, I 9, C 3, A 1, N 14, S 19.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If 'X % Y & Z', how is Z related to X?

solution.concept: The wife of one's father is one's mother
solution.explanation: X is Y's daughter and Y is Z's husband, so Z is X's mother.
steps: X % Y: X is Y's daughter
Y & Z: Z is Y's wife ⇒ X's mother
solution.why_others_wrong: Z is a generation above X, so not her sister or daughter; nothing puts her two generations above.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If 'M ! N & O', how is O related to M?

solution.concept: A son's wife is a daughter-in-law
solution.explanation: M is N's father and N is O's husband, so O is the wife of M's son: M's daughter-in-law.
steps: M ! N: N is M's son (a husband is male)
N & O: O is N's wife ⇒ daughter-in-law
solution.why_others_wrong: O is married into the family, not M's own daughter; M's wife is N's mother; O is a generation below M.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If 'R ! S % T', how is T related to R?

solution.explanation: R is S's father; S is T's daughter, so T is S's other parent, her mother. T is therefore R's wife.
steps: R ! S: R is S's father
S % T: T is S's parent ⇒ mother
Father and mother of S ⇒ T is R's wife
solution.why_others_wrong: S is the daughter; T and R are S's two parents, so T is neither R's sister nor his mother.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Usha is the mother of Vinay. Vinay is the brother of Wamiqa, and Xavier is Wamiqa's husband. How is Usha related to Xavier?

solution.explanation: Vinay and Wamiqa are siblings, so Usha is Wamiqa's mother too. Xavier is Wamiqa's husband, so Usha is his mother-in-law.
steps: Usha = mother of Vinay and Wamiqa
solution.why_others_wrong: Xavier is not Usha's own son; she is a generation above him, so not his sister-in-law; an aunt is a parent's sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Deepak is the only son of Eshwar. Geeta is Deepak's sister, and Farida is Geeta's daughter. How is Deepak related to Farida?

solution.explanation: Deepak is the brother of Farida's mother Geeta, so he is Farida's (maternal) uncle.
solution.why_others_wrong: Farida's father is Geeta's husband; Deepak is a generation above Farida, so not her brother; her grandfather is Eshwar.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Hari is the husband of Ila. Ila's only son is Jai, and Jai's wife is Kiya. Lina is Kiya's daughter. How is Hari related to Lina?

solution.explanation: Jai is the son of Hari and Ila, and Lina is the daughter of Jai and his wife Kiya. Hari is Lina's father's father: her grandfather.
steps: Lina = Jai's daughter ⇒ Hari is her grandfather
solution.why_others_wrong: Lina's father is Jai; Hari is two generations above her; he is Kiya's father-in-law, not Lina's.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Looking at the photograph of a woman, Kunal said, "Her husband's mother is the only sister of my father." How is the woman related to Kunal?

solution.concept: Collapse the phrase from the inside out
solution.explanation: The only sister of Kunal's father is Kunal's paternal aunt. Her son, the woman's husband, is Kunal's cousin, so the woman is the wife of Kunal's cousin.
solution.why_others_wrong: She is not a child of Kunal's parents; the aunt is her mother-in-law, not her; she is related to Kunal only by marriage, so not his own cousin.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Wife of his cousin

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability

options.text: A is the uncle of C
D is the husband of B
A is the son of D

solution.explanation: A is B's brother; B is C's mother; C is D's daughter, so D is C's father and B's husband. So A is C's maternal uncle, D is B's husband and C is a girl — all true. A is B's brother, i.e. D's brother-in-law, not D's son.
steps: A @ B, B # C ⇒ A is C's maternal uncle
C $ D with B the mother ⇒ D is the father, B's husband
A is D's brother-in-law ⇒ 'son of D' is false
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three statements follow directly from the code.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is the son of D

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Om is the father of Usha, and Tia is Usha's daughter. Usha's only sibling is Varun, and Wanda is Varun's wife. How is Wanda related to Tia?

solution.explanation: Varun is the brother of Tia's mother Usha, i.e. Tia's maternal uncle. Wanda, his wife, is Tia's aunt.
solution.why_others_wrong: Tia's mother is Usha; Wanda is Usha's sister-in-law, not Tia's; Tia's grandmother is Om's wife.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How is Qasim related to Pranav?

solution.explanation: Pranav's father Mehul is Naina's brother, and Qasim is Naina's husband, so Qasim is Pranav's uncle (paternal aunt's husband).
steps: Kartik + Leela → Mehul (+ Ojasvi) → Pranav; Naina (+ Qasim) → Riya
Qasim = husband of Pranav's father's sister ⇒ uncle
solution.why_others_wrong: Pranav's father is Mehul; Qasim's child Riya is Pranav's cousin; his grandfather is Kartik.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How is Leela related to Riya?

solution.explanation: Riya's mother is Naina (Qasim's wife), and Naina is Leela's daughter, so Leela is Riya's grandmother.
steps: Kartik + Leela → Mehul (+ Ojasvi) → Pranav; Naina (+ Qasim) → Riya
solution.why_others_wrong: Riya's mother is Naina; Leela is two generations above Riya; she is Qasim's mother-in-law, not Riya's.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How is Ojasvi related to Naina?

solution.explanation: Ojasvi is married to Mehul, Naina's brother, so Ojasvi is Naina's sister-in-law.
steps: Kartik + Leela → Mehul (+ Ojasvi) → Pranav; Naina (+ Qasim) → Riya
solution.why_others_wrong: Ojasvi has different parents from Naina; she is in Naina's generation, so not her mother-in-law; cousins share grandparents.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Sahil is the only son-in-law of Rohan's paternal grandfather. Rohan's father has exactly one sibling, and every person mentioned has only one spouse. How is Sahil related to Rohan?

solution.concept: A son-in-law must be married to a daughter
solution.explanation: A son-in-law of Rohan's grandfather is married to one of the grandfather's daughters. The grandfather's children are Rohan's father and his only sibling, so that sibling is a daughter: Rohan's paternal aunt. Sahil is her husband, i.e. Rohan's uncle.
steps: Only sibling of Rohan's father ⇒ that daughter
solution.why_others_wrong: Rohan's father is a son of the grandfather, not a son-in-law; Sahil is a generation above Rohan, so not his brother-in-law or cousin.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Uncle (husband of his father's sister)

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability

solution.concept: Test every option; the gender of P must be fixed
solution.explanation: In 'P ™ Q ® S', P is Q's daughter and Q is S's brother, so P is the daughter of S's brother: S's niece. In 'S ® Q © P', S is the brother of P's mother, but P's gender is unknown (nephew or niece). 'P ® Q ™ S' makes P S's son, and 'S © Q ® P' makes S P's mother.
steps: Option 1: daughter of S's brother ⇒ niece ✓
solution.why_others_wrong: The second does not fix P's gender; the third and fourth give son and mother.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Early one morning, Kavya walked straight towards the sun. She then turned to her left and kept walking. In which direction was she walking then?

solution.concept: The morning sun is in the east
solution.explanation: Walking towards the morning sun means walking east. A left turn from east points north.
solution.why_others_wrong: South is a right turn from east; West is away from the sun; East ignores the turn.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: What is the straight-line distance between the depot and stop B, and in which direction is B from the depot?

solution.explanation: B is 6 km east and 8 km north of D: √(36 + 64) = 10 km, north-east.
solution.why_others_wrong: '10 km, North-West' mixes up east and west; '10 km, South-West' gives the direction of the start from the end point; '14 km, North-East' adds the two components instead of using Pythagoras.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How far is the end point F from the depot in a straight line, and in which direction?

solution.concept: Net displacement of the whole trip
solution.explanation: East: 6 − 12 + 10 = 4 km; north: 8 − 5 = 3 km. √(16 + 9) = 5 km, north-east.
solution.why_others_wrong: '5 km, North-West' mixes up east and west; '5 km, South-West' gives the direction of the start from the end point; '7 km, North-East' adds the two components instead of using Pythagoras.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In which direction is stop C with respect to stop F?

solution.explanation: C (−6, 8) − F (4, 3) = (−10, 5): west and north, so C is north-west of F.
solution.why_others_wrong: South-East is F's direction from C; North-East misreads C as east of F; West ignores the 5 km north component.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which stop is nearest to the depot in a straight line?

solution.explanation: Distances from D: A 6 km, B 10 km, C 10 km, E √45 ≈ 6.7 km, F 5 km. F is nearest.
solution.why_others_wrong: A is 6 km, E about 6.7 km and B 10 km away.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: A girl is facing south-east. She turns 135° anticlockwise three times in a row. Which direction is she facing now?

solution.explanation: Three turns of 135° make 405° anticlockwise, which is a full circle plus 45°. 45° anticlockwise from south-east is east.
solution.why_others_wrong: North and South-West come from stopping after one or two turns; South turns the last 45° the other way.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: At about 5 pm, Anil and Bhanu were walking straight towards each other on a road. Anil's shadow fell directly behind him. In which direction was Bhanu walking?

solution.explanation: At 5 pm the sun is in the west, so shadows point east. Anil's shadow was behind him, so Anil was walking west, towards the sun. Bhanu, walking towards Anil, was walking east.
steps: Shadow behind Anil ⇒ Anil walks west
Bhanu walks the opposite way ⇒ east
solution.why_others_wrong: West is Anil's direction; North and South are at right angles to the road's direction.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Sneha cycles 7 km towards the north, turns right and cycles 5 km, turns left and cycles 4 km, turns right and cycles 9 km, and then turns right again and cycles 11 km. How far is she from her starting point, and in which direction?

solution.concept: North and south legs may cancel
solution.explanation: North 7 + 4 = 11, then south 11: the north–south parts cancel. East 5 + 9 = 14 km. She is 14 km due east of the start.
steps: Turn right from north ⇒ east: 5 km → (5, 7)
Turn left from east ⇒ north: 4 km → (5, 11)
Turn right from north ⇒ east: 9 km → (14, 11)
Turn right from east ⇒ south: 11 km → (14, 0)
solution.why_others_wrong: West mixes up the right turns; 36 km adds every leg; 11 km, South is only the last leg.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which point lies exactly midway between K and J?

solution.concept: Drop M onto the line KJ
solution.explanation: M = (5, 5) is the midpoint of KL. N is 5 m south of M, i.e. (5, 0), which is exactly halfway along KJ from (0, 0) to (10, 0).
solution.why_others_wrong: M is 5 m north of KJ, O is 2 m west of K's north–south line, and L is 10 m north of J.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: What is the straight-line distance between K and M, and in which direction is M from K?

solution.explanation: M is the midpoint of KL, and L is 10 m east and 10 m north of K, so M is 5 m east and 5 m north of K: 5√2 m, north-east.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 m, North ignores the east part; 10 m takes the full side length; South-West is K's direction from M.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How far is L from O, and in which direction is L from O?

solution.explanation: O = (−2, 5) and L = (10, 10): L is 12 m east and 5 m north of O, √(144 + 25) = 13 m, north-east.
solution.why_others_wrong: South-West is O's direction from L; 17 m adds the two parts; 12 m, East ignores the north part.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In a certain code language, SALT is written as WEPX. How is CORN written in that code language?

solution.concept: Every letter moves forward by the same number of places
solution.explanation: S→W, A→E, L→P, T→X: every letter moves 4 places forward. C→G, O→S, R→V, N→R: GSVR.
solution.why_others_wrong: YKNJ moves the letters back; GSVQ moves N only 3 places; HTWS moves every letter 5 places.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In a certain code, 5274 is written as 6385 and 3916 is written as 4027. How is 8093 written in that code?

steps: Each digit +1, keeping only the units digit
solution.why_others_wrong: 7982 subtracts 1; 9105 adds 2 to the last digit; 3909 reverses the number and changes nothing else.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In a certain code, LEMON is written as LMKCJ and GRAPE is written as CNYPE. How is MELON written in that code?

solution.concept: Reverse, then move each letter back
solution.explanation: LEMON reversed is NOMEL; each letter moved 2 places back: L M K C J. GRAPE → EPARG → C N Y P E. MELON → NOLEM → L M J C K.
solution.why_others_wrong: KCJML shifts without reversing; PQNGO moves the letters forward; LMJCL moves the last letter back only once.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In a certain code, 4815 is written as 3366 and 2967 is written as 8547. How is 7302 written in that code?

solution.concept: Swap the halves, then +2 and −2 alternately
solution.explanation: 4815: the two halves are interchanged → 1548; then the 1st and 3rd digits get +2 and the 2nd and 4th get −2: 3 3 6 6. 2967 → 6729 → 8 5 4 7. 7302 → 0273 → 0+2 = 2, 2−2 = 0, 7+2 = 9, 3−2 = 1: 2091.
solution.why_others_wrong: 9180 applies the +2/−2 without swapping; 0273 only swaps; 2093 adds 2 to the last digit.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How is 'BRIDGE' written in this code?

solution.explanation: BRIDGE: last letter E, 6 letters, B + 2 = D, giving E6D. Six is even, so the code is reversed: D6E.
solution.why_others_wrong: E6D forgets the reversal; D6F reverses but shifts the wrong letter; E6B does not shift B.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How is 'STAMP' written in this code?

solution.explanation: STAMP: last letter P, 5 letters, S + 2 = U. Five is odd, so the code stays P5U.
solution.why_others_wrong: U5P reverses an odd-length code; P5T moves S only one place; R5U shifts the last letter.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which of the following words is written as 'K7R' in this code?

solution.explanation: K7R is not reversed only if the word has an odd number of letters: 7 letters, ending in K, with first letter R − 2 = P. PADLOCK fits. SHAMROCK → U8K, PARK → R4K, PLUCK → K5R.
steps: Last letter K, first letter P, 7 letters ⇒ PADLOCK
solution.why_others_wrong: SHAMROCK has 8 letters and starts with S; PARK has 4 letters (code reversed); PLUCK has 5.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which element is 3rd to the left of the 6th element from the right end?

solution.concept: Convert a right-end position, then move left
solution.explanation: The 6th from the right is the 12th from the left (F). Three places to its left is the 9th element: K.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many numbers in the arrangement are immediately followed by a letter?

solution.concept: Look at the right neighbour of every number
solution.explanation: Numbers and their right neighbours: 3 %, 8 A, 5 K, 1 F, 7 I, 2 Y. Followed by a letter: 8 A, 5 K, 1 F, 7 I, 2 Y — 5.
steps: Keep those with a letter on the right

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If all the numbers are removed from the arrangement, which element will be 7th from the left end?

solution.explanation: Without numbers: W % H A @ K £ F I # Y. The 7th from the left is £.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Which term should replace the question mark in the series?

C3, F6, I9, L12, ?

solution.concept: The number is the letter's position
solution.explanation: The letters move 3 places forward each time (C, F, I, L, O) and each number is its letter's position (3, 6, 9, 12, 15). The next term is O15.
solution.why_others_wrong: O14 and N15 break the link between the letter and its position; P15 moves the letter 4 places.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Study the following arrangement of letters, numbers and symbols and answer the question.

T % A 6 # E @ 9 U $ R I ¥ 4 O & B

How many vowels in the arrangement are immediately followed by a symbol?

solution.concept: Look at the right neighbour of every vowel
solution.explanation: Vowels and their right neighbours: A 6, E @, U $, I ¥, O &. Followed by a symbol: E @, U $, I ¥, O & — 4.
steps: Vowels: A, E, U, I, O
Keep those with a symbol on the right

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If every letter in the arrangement is replaced by the letter that comes immediately after it in the English alphabet, how many vowels will the new arrangement contain?

solution.concept: Only letters just before a vowel become vowels
solution.explanation: A letter becomes a vowel only if it is D, H, N, T or Z (→ E, I, O, U, A). Letters of the arrangement: M, D, U, S, E, K, V, A, Z, H, O. Of these, D, Z, H become vowels — 3.
steps: Letters before vowels: D, H, N, T, Z

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many symbols are there between the 2nd vowel from the left end and the 3rd number from the right end?

solution.explanation: 2nd vowel from the left: E (10th). 3rd number from the right: 3 (16th). Between them: # K 9 V £. Symbols: #, £ — 2.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which element is 7th to the right of the element that lies exactly midway between the 2nd and the 12th elements from the left end?

solution.explanation: Midway between the 2nd and 12th is the (2 + 12) ÷ 2 = 7th element (©). Seven places to its right is the 14th element: V.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If all the symbols are removed and then the first twelve of the remaining elements are written in reverse order, which element will be 7th from the right end?

solution.concept: Delete, then reverse a block, then count
solution.explanation: Without symbols (23 elements): 5 Q E 8 J 2 I N 7 T 4 O P 3 G A 9 L 6 K U 1 R. Reversing the first twelve: O 4 T 7 N I 2 J 8 E Q 5 P 3 G A 9 L 6 K U 1 R. The 7th from the right is 9.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many letters in the arrangement are immediately preceded by a symbol and immediately followed by an even number?

solution.explanation: Letters with a symbol on the left: @ E 8, # T 4, & O P, £ G A, ¥ L 6, * U 1. Of these, followed by an even number: @ E 8, # T 4, ¥ L 6 — 3.
steps: Find letters with a symbol on the left
Keep those with an even number on the right

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If all the consonants are removed from the arrangement, which element will be 4th to the right of the 5th element from the left end?

solution.explanation: Without consonants: 5 @ E 8 % 2 I 7 # 4 & O 3 £ A 9 ¥ 6 * U 1. The 5th element is %; four places to its right is the 9th: #.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: What is the difference between the sum of the numbers that are immediately preceded by a vowel and the sum of the numbers that are immediately followed by a vowel?

solution.explanation: Preceded by a vowel: 8, 9, 1 (sum 18). Followed by a vowel: 2 (sum 2). Difference: 16.
steps: Numbers with a vowel on the left
Numbers with a vowel on the right
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options are one of the two sums alone, or their total.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many times does a number stand exactly two places to the right of a vowel (with one element in between)?

solution.concept: Check the element two places to the right of every vowel
solution.explanation: Each vowel with the element two places to its right: E … J, I … 7, O … 3, A … ¥, U … R. Numbers there: I N 7, O P 3 — 2.
steps: Vowels: E, I, O, A, U
Look two places to the right of each

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many letters of the word have a position in the English alphabet that is a prime number?

solution.explanation: Positions: R 18, E 5, P 16, U 21, B 2, L 12, I 9, C 3, A 1, N 14, S 19. Prime positions: E (5), B (2), C (3), S (19) — 4.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which letter is 3rd to the right of the letter that lies exactly midway between the 1st and 9th letters of the word?

solution.explanation: Midway between the 1st and 9th letters is the 5th letter, B. Three places to its right is the 8th letter: C.
solution.why_others_wrong: I is 7th and A 9th; L is only one place to the right of B.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many pairs of letters in the word have as many letters between them in the word as in the English alphabet (counting both forward and backward)?

solution.concept: Compare the gap in the word with the gap in the alphabet
solution.explanation: Pairs found: RP, RU, EB — 3 in all.
steps: Positions: R 18, E 5, P 16, U 21, B 2, L 12, I 9, C 3, A 1, N 14, S 19
A pair qualifies when |word gap| = |alphabet gap|

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which letter is as many places to the right of P in the English alphabet as K is to the right of D?

solution.concept: Find the gap, then apply it
solution.explanation: K (11) is 7 places to the right of D (4). Seven places to the right of P (16) is the 23rd letter: W.
solution.why_others_wrong: V and X are 6 and 8 places from P; I is 7 places to the left of P.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If the words MANAGE, MANAGER, MANAGING and MANAGEMENT are arranged in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary, which word will be third?

solution.concept: A shorter word that is the start of a longer one comes first
solution.explanation: MANAGE comes first, being the beginning of the others. MANAGEMENT and MANAGER both start with MANAGE; their next letters are M and R, so MANAGEMENT comes before MANAGER. MANAGING (I after MANAG, and I > E) comes last. Third: MANAGER.
solution.why_others_wrong: MANAGEMENT is second, MANAGING fourth and MANAGE first.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: If all the vowels are removed from the English alphabet, which letter will be 12th from the right end of the remaining letters?

solution.explanation: Without A, E, I, O, U, 21 letters remain. The 12th from the right is the 21 − 12 + 1 = 10th from the left: B C D F G H J K L M — M.
steps: 12th from the right = 10th from the left
solution.why_others_wrong: L and N are one place off; O is a vowel and has been removed.
